desc:
Imagine text written around a circle, so that after its last character comes its first character again. For a start index i (0 ≤ i < n), read m consecutive characters clockwise from i, wrapping around the end when needed. Count the start indices for which the characters read equal pattern.

Example: text = "abaab" and pattern = "aba". Starting at 0 gives "aba" and starting at 3 gives "ab" followed by the wrapped-around "a", which is "aba" as well. The answer is 2.
constraints: Both strings consist of lowercase English letters
hints: Building each of the n windows by taking indices modulo n and comparing is O(n · m).
Occurrences that wrap around the end are ordinary occurrences in a longer, unrolled string.

Search for pattern in text + text[:m-1] with KMP (or the Z-function) and count the matches. Every start index 0..n-1 is covered exactly once, with no double counting, because the extended string has length n + m - 1.
editorial: Unroll the circle. A window starting at index i that does not wrap is a window of text; one that wraps reads the tail of text and then a prefix of it. Both kinds are windows of t = text + text[:m-1], which has n + m - 1 characters and therefore exactly n windows of length m, starting at 0..n-1: one per circular start.

Because m ≤ n, the extra m - 1 characters never need to wrap a second time. Count the occurrences of the pattern in t with KMP: build pi of the pattern, scan t, and count every time the matched length reaches m, falling back by pi[m-1] afterwards.
O(n + m) time, O(n + m) space. A common alternative is to pass over text + text, but then you must stop after n start positions to avoid counting a window twice.
